tasks.short: Confirm supplier shipment quantities, dates and references, then resolve discrepancies and update production planning.

steps.what: Identify shipments needing confirmation against purchase orders and production requirements.
Ask suppliers to confirm dispatch dates, quantities and shipment references.
Check supplier confirmations against purchase order quantities and required delivery dates.

loop.input: Supplier confirmation text and attachments, with purchase order references.
loop.output: Proposed shipment fields, source excerpts and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units and dates against the purchase order; clerk approves accepted fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per confirmation; unresolved fields enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier prose and attachment layouts vary. Structured portal responses bypass the model.

steps.what: Discuss missing details or delays and agree escalation with the supplier.
Record confirmed shipment details and notify production planning of material changes.

tasks.design: Configure a confirmation queue in the {PROCUREMENT} and send approved factual requests through the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded extractor proposes fields from supplier replies; clerk-approved details update the {OPS_SYSTEM} and trigger planning notifications. Supplier calls remain human, supported by a concise discrepancy brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier replies lack consistent fields, and purchase orders and production dates sit in separate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing request templates and field validation handle routine work. AI-assisted coding makes the connector cheaper; bounded extraction handles varied replies.
tasks.still_hard: A promised date may be unreliable. Recovering from shortages requires supplier trust and production trade-offs.
tasks.human_edge: Judge supplier credibility, uncover unstated delays and negotiate recovery without making unauthorised commitments.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time chasing routine confirmations and more time resolving credible shortage risks. They can gain authority to trigger a shortage review; purchasing commitments remain with the purchasing role.

reach.task: Assess which late inbound shipments threaten the next production shift.
reach.learn: Lead-time variability, shipment milestones and material criticality.

evidence.claim: Qargo extracts PDF orders into fields. This supports the extraction pattern, not shipment-confirmation accuracy.
Queues, templated requests and approved field updates can use deterministic workflow rules.

assumptions: Scope is one site's inbound shipments with stable purchase order identifiers.
Automatic requests only ask for facts; they do not change orders or accept revised commercial terms.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
GDPR applies to supplier contact data. Access work includes applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which suppliers provide structured confirmations or portal access?
Can shipment fields be written through supported interfaces?
Who may accept revised delivery dates or escalate shortages?
research_questions: Can existing confirmation features remove the need for a custom connector?
Which date and quantity checks catch ambiguous supplier replies before acceptance?
new_work: Review extracted shipment fields and resolve unmatched references.
Maintain request templates, reminder limits and contact records.
Monitor failed updates and reconcile duplicate supplier replies.

tasks.short: Record production quantities, material consumption and quality measurements against production orders.

steps.what: Collect shift sheets containing output, material consumption and quality measurements.
Check order references, units and totals against production records.
Resolve missing counts, unexplained consumption or questionable measurements with the shift supervisor.
Enter validated quantities, consumption and measurements against the production order.
Approve quality measurements and record any required quality disposition.
Copy approved totals into a parallel production summary workbook.

tasks.design: Configure structured shift capture in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with order identifiers, unit checks and required fields. A deterministic connector records validated submissions and routes discrepancies to the clerk; quality disposition retains its approval gate. An existing {OPS_SYSTEM} report replaces the duplicate workbook.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper capture, inconsistent units and delayed corrections make automatic posting unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured entry and existing validation features remove most transcription. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting capture to production records.
tasks.still_hard: Software cannot establish whether a physical count or measurement was taken correctly. Scrap, rework and backdated corrections need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Find the physical cause of discrepancies and distinguish recording errors from genuine production or quality problems.

ambition.what: Within-shift review of abnormal material consumption

tasks.altitude: The clerk works from a discrepancy queue instead of entering shift totals. They can gain authority to request an immediate consumption check; quality disposition remains with the quality lead.

reach.task: Investigate recurring gaps between material consumption, good output and scrap.
reach.learn: Measurement traceability, yield calculations and quality disposition codes.

evidence.claim: Structured production capture, unit validation and duplicate-safe posting can use deterministic software.
The digest provides no documented manufacturing production-recording case for this proposed design.

assumptions: The baseline represents a plant using paper shift sheets alongside the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Operators enter measurements at source; this creates operator capture work and requires rollout support.
Duplicate workbook removal assumes an existing report meets its users' needs.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for one site.
GDPR applies to identifiable operator records. National rules may require consultation over changed work practices or monitoring.
unknowns: Are shift measurements already captured digitally?
Which fields affect stock valuation, payroll or regulated quality records?
Does the {OPS_SYSTEM} support corrections with an audit history?
Which consultation and device-access requirements apply?
research_questions: Can native capture forms and interfaces cover the required production fields?
How should duplicate submissions, late entries and reversals be tested against inventory balances?
new_work: Operators capture structured shift data at source.
Review validation failures and unexplained consumption.
Maintain units, material mappings and tolerance rules.
Reconcile connector failures and audit corrections.

tasks.short: Prepare approved production directions, resource requirements, work locations and cost projections.

steps.what: Retrieve approved specifications, drawings and previous work instructions.
Calculate materials, tools, equipment, labour requirements and projected costs.
Confirm work locations, practical sequencing and resource availability with production supervisors.
Assemble construction directions, work locations, resource lists and cost projections into a draft pack.

loop.input: Approved source instructions, calculated requirements and confirmed feasibility notes.
loop.output: Draft explanatory directions with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Lock calculated tables; compare instruction references and flag unsupported directions for engineering review.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per pack; missing or conflicting instructions go to the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative instructions vary across products. Fixed tables and established instruction templates remain deterministic.

steps.what: Validate technical directions and approve the work pack for production use.
Attach the approved work pack to production orders and notify supervisors.

tasks.design: A generator combines approved revisions from the {DOCS}, resource data from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and cost rates from the {ERP}. Deterministic calculations produce resource and cost tables; a bounded drafting loop assembles source-linked narrative directions. Engineering approval releases the versioned pack to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, routing data and cost rates are fragmented. Practical production knowledge is often held by supervisors.
tasks.enabler_now: Version-controlled sources and reusable calculation templates already support much of the work. AI-assisted coding and bounded drafting reduce assembly effort.
tasks.still_hard: New production methods, safety-critical directions and realistic labour estimates require engineering knowledge and physical validation.
tasks.human_edge: Spot instructions that are technically plausible but impractical on the shop floor, and reconcile competing resource constraints.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking build readiness with supervisors and less time assembling documents. They can gain authority to request a readiness review; engineering retains approval of construction directions.

reach.task: Prepare the resource readiness checkpoint for a prototype build.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, change control and resource estimates.

evidence.claim: Approved bills of materials, routings and rates support deterministic resource and cost calculations.
Source-linked drafting can assist document assembly but does not establish technical correctness.

assumptions: The clerk prepares documentation from approved engineering inputs rather than designing manufacturing methods.
The first release covers one product family and its existing instruction templates.
Headcount estimates use approved labour standards, not predictions about individual workers.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies where records identify workers. Changes to working-time arrangements may require consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Are bills of materials, routings and drawings version-controlled and mutually consistent?
Who approves technical directions, cost assumptions and labour standards?
Which instructions require formal safety or regulatory validation?
Can approved packs be attached to production orders through supported interfaces?
research_questions: How much narrative assembly can existing templates eliminate?
Which checks detect obsolete revisions and unsupported construction directions?
new_work: Review generated narrative and resolve source conflicts.
Maintain templates, calculation rules and approved source mappings.
Test revision handling and withdraw superseded packs.
Compare projected requirements with actual build results.

tasks.short: File operational documents, link them to records and keep them complete, retrievable and correctly retained.

steps.what: Collect maintenance records, bills of lading and cost reports from departmental mailboxes.
Check document completeness and match documents to shipments, assets or production orders.

loop.input: Unstructured operational documents and permitted reference records.
loop.output: Proposed document type, identifiers and record links, with source excerpts.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against reference records; clerk approves inferred links. Exact structured matches bypass review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; ambiguous links remain unfiled in an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some documents lack consistent metadata or layouts. Existing identifiers are matched deterministically first.

steps.what: Scan paper originals using a scanner and check page completeness.
Name files, store documents and update links in the operational records.
Request missing documents from departmental owners.
Approve retention or disposal after checking retention periods and legal holds.

tasks.design: Connect designated {EMAIL} folders and operational exports to a controlled register in the {DOCS}. Deterministic rules handle known references, naming and reminders; a bounded extractor proposes metadata for irregular documents, with clerk approval of inferred links. Retention rules produce a disposal preview, checked against legal holds and approved before deletion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive through separate channels with weak identifiers. Retention decisions and legal holds are not consistently connected to filing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata, versioning and retention features cover much of the register. AI-assisted coding lowers connector effort, and bounded extraction helps with irregular documents.
tasks.still_hard: Paper originals, missing signatures, disputed versions and legally required retention need explicit handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a document is incomplete, unreliable or subject to a dispute, and secure the authoritative record.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time naming and moving files and more time resolving evidence gaps. They can gain authority to assemble audit packets; disposal approval remains with the records manager.

reach.task: Reconcile delivery evidence with shipment and receipt records.
reach.learn: Shipment identifiers, proof-of-delivery requirements and document provenance.

reach.task: Check that asset maintenance evidence is complete before an inspection.
reach.learn: Asset registers, maintenance intervals and required inspection records.

evidence.claim: Qargo with TransFollow creates and signs electronic consignment notes inside a transport system.
The digest notes that paper consignment notes may still be needed abroad; paper handling cannot universally disappear.
Metadata registers, controlled access, retention previews and duplicate detection can use existing document features and deterministic rules.

assumptions: The initial scope covers selected document classes at one site.
Source-generated digital documents reduce scanning; remaining paper originals still receive completeness checks.
Deletion requires approval and a current legal hold check.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to personal data in documents. Retention periods and employee consultation depend partly on national rules.
unknowns: Which document classes require paper originals or specific retention periods?
Where are legal holds recorded, and who approves disposal?
How many documents lack reliable order, shipment or asset identifiers?
Which mailboxes and record stores may the connector access?
research_questions: Can native document metadata and retention features cover the initial scope?
Which matching thresholds prevent documents being linked to the wrong order?
How should missing pages, superseded versions and duplicate scans be detected?
new_work: Review uncertain document links and incomplete scans.
Maintain document classes, retention schedules and access groups.
Approve disposal previews and reconcile legal holds.
Monitor connector failures and audit document provenance.

role.altitude: The role moves toward material readiness, production discrepancy resolution and reliable operational evidence. Proposed decision rights cover initiating shortage and consumption reviews and assembling readiness or audit packs; purchasing, engineering, quality and disposal approvals stay with their accountable roles.
reach: Logistics analysis of inbound delays and production exposure.
Quality investigation of consumption, output and scrap discrepancies.
Project readiness checks for prototype builds.
skills_to_grow: Production order, material and shipment data relationships.
Unit validation, yield calculations and correction traceability.
Supplier escalation and practical production constraints.
Document revision control, retention and provenance.
Reviewing source-linked extraction and drafting outputs.
role.ambitious_version: Provide shift-start material risk reviews, within-shift consumption alerts and engineering-approved prototype readiness packs from a shared operational record. Start with reusable templates and validation rules; connect live systems once the employer grants access.
